§7.2.11 Superscript and Subscript

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-superscript-and-subscript · text formatting inline

✅ Normative

Raised and lowered text outside maths MUST be written with <sup> and <sub>. A Unicode superscript or subscript character MUST NOT be substituted for the tag.

H<sub>2</sub>O        ← conforming
H₂O                   ← non-conforming

The same applies to superscripts: x<sup>2</sup>, not x². Inside an equation, raised and lowered terms are LaTeX ^{…} and _{…} within $$ … $$ — see Inline Equations§7.2.6.

Why the tag

A tag round-trips: a reader can strip it, render it, or read the base character underneath. A Unicode glyph is lossy in the other direction — ₂ does not compare equal to 2, so a downstream numeric parse or string match silently fails. Unicode also has no raised or lowered form for most characters, so substitution cannot be applied consistently.

Inside table cells

A footnote superscript attached to a value — 48,210³ — MUST be tagged as 48,210<sup>3</sup>. Whether the marker stays in the cell is a separate question, answered by Marks and Symbols in Cells§9.6.6.

A raised marker that is itself Markdown punctuation is tagged and escaped: <sup>\*\*</sup> — see Escaping Printed Marks§7.2.4.
